correctness.rationale: The area and spectrum normalizations are verified from polar integration. A positive gap e^{-t}t²/2 isolates occupied monomials 0,1. The analytic coherent-state projector density yields trace-class third-order Taylor control. The exact cluster Rayleigh–Schrödinger second coefficient consists of a direct term -t e^{-t}∑_{k≥1}|hhat_k|² and cross-cluster ratios e^{-t}(t|hhat_1|²+∑_{k≥2}(a_k/Σ_{1..k}a_j+t a_{k+1}/Σ_{2..k+1}a_j)|hhat_k|²), giving zero mode k=1 and stated Dk. The two ratios decrease strictly with k by exact falling-factorial denominators, proving Dk strictly increasing and sharp D2=t(3+2t)/((t+2)(t+3)). The packaged checker independently passed 24 finite-section tests over three t values; tests corroborate but do not prove the infinite statement. No uniform-in-h or global-optimizing assertion is made.

originality.rationale: Statement/implication comparisons distinguish rank-two nonradial shape Hessian from known Gaussian disk eigenvalues, rank-one STFT Faber–Krahn stability, radial K-sum isoperimetry and existence of global K-sum optimizers. The 2025 primary text explicitly leaves the nonradial inequality open, and its radial proof cannot imply the new nonradial Fourier spectrum. Searches and relevant full-text sections revealed no equivalent prior statement; historical-priority uncertainty remains.
residual_risks: Unindexed historical perturbation calculations, including shape derivatives stated without Fock/Toeplitz keywords, might cover a special or equivalent formulation.

Mathematical correctness and publication priority have not been independently audited.

value.rationale: The first-two-eigenvalue Ky-Fan sum measures optimal concentration of an orthonormal pair, a central quantity of accumulated spectrograms and the later open nonradial sum-isoperimetry problem. The result proves positive curvature for every nontranslation Fourier shape direction and identifies exactly the unique lowest positive angular frequency and its sharp coefficient. It establishes a natural infinite-dimensional structural local stability theorem rather than a routine known-table evaluation. Global stability is deliberately not claimed.
